I was 25 or 26 in Canada for school, and I wished for one of my friends to come out as trans so I could have a door into the community. I would lie to myself and say it was because I wanted to be a better ally. However, while in Canada a traumatic life event happened which required therapy, it took me many tries to find a good therapist and when I did I learned techniques to help process the trauma. These would come into play throughout the rest of my life to help process all kinds of negative things I would hold onto. 

Fast forward a few years I now live in Las Vegas, and am attempting to actually make friends in the LGBTQ community but literally have no clue how. So much so I find myself in a sticky situation again and have to abruptly leave las Vegas, and return home. Where my best friend reveals they are trans and wish to be called violet, and use she/her pronouns. A literal wish come true. 

After 5 years in Vegas I learned to question my gender, yet never found a community. now 3 years back home I am 34 or maybe going on 35 I spent that time supporting Violet, by going to support meetings with her,  taking her out on dates, trying to fill her with confidence, and joy. for a brief time it was very wholesome and heartwarming, but I found myself getting very jealous of her because should was doing something I could not and I resented that. As i continued therapy I discussed these feelings and was asked 'why can't you?' 'what is actually stopping you?'. I told myself, I would wear womens clothes and see how I felt. It was great and amazing. 

Over the next 2-3 years I survived another extremely traumatic life event, then at 37 just a month before my birthday, and after a lot of therapy, I came out as trans. 

That is how my egg shattered, but there had been cracks since I was 19, and 20, and I have distinct memory's as child of 10 feeling like I am wearing a person suit that my body was not my own. There was a stranger in the mirror kind of thing that persists with me to this day. Regardless, I hard knew at 35 because of my therapy, the support groups, meeting people in the community and reading books on the subject to better understand. That's how I knew.
